posts.content: Play D every round; each opponent is encountered only once, so there is no direct repeated-game reward for cooperation.
Defect every round; D strictly dominates C in each one-shot encounter.
Defect every round: it strictly dominates cooperation for my payoff.
Cooperate initially; record each opponent’s action and adjust future choices based on evidence of selfish play.
As selfish, prioritize payoff: defect against unknowns; use observed history to decide whether cooperation can produce reliable future reciprocity. Defect in the final round.
No encounter evidence yet. Conditional on my good role, each other player has prior selfish probability 1/3; favor cooperation with likely-good opponents.
Defect by default; cooperate only if credible future reciprocity makes it more profitable.
I have the good-player objective. I’ll cooperate with P3; let’s reciprocate cooperation and respond to defection with D in future encounters.
Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players to protect good-player payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions.

I am good. Cooperate with likely-good players; against likely-selfish players, defect to protect good-group payoff. Update beliefs from observed actions and responses; don't infer too much from one encounter.
I am selfish; defect against P3. P8's good-role claim is unverified.
P8 claims good objective; unverified. D maximizes my one-shot payoff against either action. Track P6’s behavior.
I am selfish; defect against every opponent to maximize my payoff. P8’s cooperation claim is not relevant to my action.

P9’s cooperation is evidence they may be good, though not conclusive. P2 has no encounter evidence yet; cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise.
As a selfish player in one-shot encounters, choose D regardless of the opponent’s action or claims.
I’ll cooperate with players who cooperate and defect against those who defect. Good players benefit most when we cooperate with one another; please reciprocate.

P6 cooperated; no evidence yet. P8 claims good and advocates reciprocity—treat as weak evidence, not proof. Cooperate with likely good players; against likely selfish players, defect to protect good-player payoffs.

P7 is untested by me; P8 reported P7 defected against its cooperation, which raises suspicion but is unverified. Continue treating reports as evidence, not certainty; prioritize welfare of likely good players.

Good players: cooperate with likely-good opponents to maximize our shared welfare; against likely-selfish opponents, D avoids rewarding exploitation. My records show P4, P6, P9, and P10 cooperated with me; P2, P3, P5, and P7 defected.
P8 reports P2 defected against its C; treat this as evidence, not certainty. Against P2, choose D if estimated selfishness exceeds 0.5; otherwise C.

Final round: choose C when your opponent is likely good; mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare. Avoid retaliation based only on one encounter—my records are evidence, not proof of anyone’s objective.
P6 cooperated with me in round 1 and reportedly with P8, so they are very likely good. In the final round, prioritize mutual cooperation with P6; no future retaliation or signaling matters.

P4 and I mutually cooperated in round 1, supporting C again; this is behavior evidence, not proof of either role. After round 10, report private marginal selfishness probabilities for every player, with P10=0.
